channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Iran says MoU with US requires finalization by relevant authorities
item.description: Iran’s Mehr news agency has reported in the European trade on Friday that the draft with the United States (US) regarding the permanent peace deal needs finalization by relevant authorities.

item.title: Euro: ECB path tied to Middle East risks – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman reports that renewed optimism over a US-Iran deal has lifted the Euro against the Dollar, with EUR/USD moving back toward 1.1600.

item.title: Japanese Yen gives away gains with markets awaiting clarity on Iran’s war
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) is giving away previous gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, with the USD/JPY pair returning to levels above 160.00, widely considered as the limit of tolerable yen weakness for Japanese authorities.

item.title: ECB’s Kocher: Too early to predict July’s interest rate decision
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member Martin Kocher stated in the European trade on Friday that it is too early to discuss what the central bank will do in the July meeting.

item.title: Brent: Gradual decline extends with lower targets – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux and colleagues note Brent has fallen below $90 per barrel after US-Iran deal hopes and President Trump’s cancelled strikes. Their technical view highlights a sustained downtrend after losing the 50-DMA and breaking an ascending trend line.

item.title: British Pound remains on the front foot vs a broadly weaker JPY after unimpressive UK data
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross regains positive traction following the previous day's good two-way price moves and sticks to intraday gains through the first half of the European session on Friday.

item.title: ECB's Makhlouf: The central bank needs to get ahead of inflation
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member and Governor of the Central Bank of Ireland, Gabriel Makhlouf, said during the European trade on Friday that the central bank needs to act quickly before inflation starts accelerating further.

item.title: Japanese Yen trades back to intervention levels despite widely-expected BoJ hike
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) continues to face substantial downside pressure, trading at highly elevated levels against the US Dollar and crossing historical intervention-trigger points.

item.title: Euro gains against Japanese Yen on more ECB interest rate hike hopes
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades higher 0.12% higher to near 185.45 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) during the European trading session on Friday.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Policy support limits downside risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Moses Lim note that the Indian Rupee has weakened sharply versus the Dollar in 2026 on higher Oil prices, portfolio outflows and a stronger USD.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Trades above 0.7950 after rebounding from nine-day EMA support
item.description: USD/CHF rebounds after registering modest losses in the previous day, trading around 0.7960 during the European hours on Friday. The technical analysis of the daily chart indicates the pair is remaining within the ascending channel pattern, signaling an ongoing bullish bias.

item.title: S&P 500: Equities jump on lower Oil and rates repricing – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists note a strong rally in US equities, with the S&P 500 posting its largest gain in two months as falling Oil prices and reduced Fed hike expectations improved the near-term outlook.

item.title: Indian Rupee rebounds as oil price plummets on US-Iran deal hopes
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens sharply higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday.

item.title: Dow Jones futures steady on Middle East uncertainty, awaits SpaceX mega IPO
item.description: Dow Jones futures remain steady around 50,880 during the European hours on Friday, ahead of the US regular opening. However, S&P 500 futures inch lower 0.09% to near 7,390, and Nasdaq 100 futures lose 0.29 %, trading near 29,380 at the time of writing.

item.title: Gold remains depressed below $4,200 amid Iran risks, Fed hike bets, USD strength
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its offered tone below the $4,200 mark through the early European session on Friday, though it holds above the lowest level since November, touched the previous day.

item.title: Euro edges down from weekly highs as markets ponder chances of a US-Iran deal
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is trading moderately lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, changing hands at 1.1565 at the time of writing, down from the weekly highs, at 1.1590 hit on Thursday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Volatile swings keep JPY range-bound against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/JPY’s brief spike to 160.69 followed by a drop to 159.64 has left the intraday outlook mixed, with trading expected between 159.70 and 160.40.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar weakens below 0.5850 as hot US PPI lifts US Dollar
item.description: The NZD/USD pair attracts some sellers to around 0.5820 during the early European trading hours on Friday. The US Dollar (USD) edges higher against the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) on hot US Producer Price Index (PPI) inflation data.

item.title: United States Dollar Index advances amid prevailing risk aversion, hawkish Fed outlook
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is holding gains after registering modest losses in the previous day and trading around 99.80 during the early European hours on Friday.

item.title: Brent: Ceasefire risks keep upside in focus – ING
item.description: ING analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey say Brent has fallen below $90/bbl on renewed hopes for a ceasefire and resumption of energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: British Pound responds slightly positive to 0.1% decline in UK GDP in April
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) attracts slight bids against its major currency peers after the release of the United Kingdom (UK) monthly Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data for April. The GBP/USD claws back a majority of its early losses and rebounds to near 1.3410.

item.title: Equities: Risk rally on Iran de‑escalation hopes – Danske Bank
item.description: According to Danske Research Team, global equities rallied strongly as investors reacted to signs of a potential US‑Iran peace agreement that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and curb nuclear ambitions.

item.title: Euro steadies against British Pound following UK GDP, German HICP inflation data
item.description: EUR/GBP inches lower after two days of gains, trading around 0.8630 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency cross remains subdued following the release of economic data from the United Kingdom (UK) and Germany.

item.title: Euro: Complex rate path questions for EUR – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen notes the European Central Bank sounded slightly hawkish, but investors already price in two further hikes, leaving the Euro softer after President Lagarde avoided clear guidance.

item.title: Canadian Dollar softens on strong US PPI data, US-Iran peace deal uncertainty
item.description: The USD/CAD pair gains traction to near 1.3980 during the early European trading hours on Friday, bolstered by hot US inflation data. Traders will closely monitor the developments surrounding the US-Iran peace deal.

item.title: British Pound: Bullish bias within higher band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann observe that GBP/USD’s surge to 1.3434 has stretched short-term conditions, but further gains toward a retest of 1.3435 remain possible, with 1.3465 unlikely to break.

item.title: Germany’s final Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices for May remains at 2.7% YoY: What it means for EUR/USD?
item.description: Germany’s final Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) data for May has arrived at 2.7% Year-on-Year (YoY), as the preliminary data showed. The inflation data cooled down from 2.9% in April. On a monthly basis, it is confirmed that the German HICP growth declined by 0.1%.

item.title: United Kingdom GDP declines by 0.1% MoM in April, as expected
item.description: The UK Gross Domestic Product (GDP) contracted by 0.1% MoM in April, following a 0.3% rise reported in March, the latest data published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) showed on Friday.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Needs decisive break above 50% Fibo retracement at 0.7050 for more upside
item.description: The AUD/USD pair is down 0.22% to near 0.7035 in the early European trade on Friday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD could rebound toward $67.00 amid potential bullish reversal
item.description: XAG/USD edges lower after registering over 6% gains in the previous day, trading around $67.00 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Friday. The technical analysis of the daily chart shows a falling wedge pattern, which suggests a strong bullish reversal.
